newsitem.title: USA: Silver to decide on N.Y. governor race by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Silver to decide on N.Y. governor race by year-end.

text.p: New York state Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, a Manhattan Democrat, on Thursday said that he would decide by the end of the year on whether to enter the gubernatorial race against the Republican incumbent.

"Before the end of the year would be the appropriate time, and I think the appropriate time for the Democratic Party to coalesce around a candidate as we start 1998," Silver said during an interview with Reuter Financial Television, when asked when he might make a decision.
"Right now, I think it is important for me to focus on the budget," he said.

New York state's budget was due on April 1, but differences between the Democrat-led Assembly and the Republican-controlled Senate, and between Democrats and Gov. George Pataki, have delayed an agreement. Issues standing in the way of a pact range from rent control to welfare reform.
Silver made it clear that he thought the state Democratic Party had a wealth of potential challengers to Pataki.
